cs.t: If you like the sound of the Juno and don’t want to pay vintage synth prices for one, I highly recommend the Behringer DeepMind. It is clearly modeled after the Juno, and adds a lot of nice features (2 DCOs per voice, 2 more-capable LFOs, an arpeggiator, full FX suite...) and you can get the 12-voice keyboard model for about half of what you’d pay for a Juno 106. It’s got a big screen in the middle, but the front panel is designed so that you almost never have to use it, even when building patches.  They have a great shortcut system for assigning modulation that’s easy to pick up and very fast to use.  It’s just a great synth all around.
